title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection sensitivity and add hysteresis rollout guard
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Our performance canary system occasionally triggers noisy rollouts for transient latency spikes (e.g. short-lived GC pauses, autoscaler jitter). This PR improves automated detection sensitivity and introduces a hysteresis-based rollout guard to reduce false positives while preserving fast detection for sustained regressions.

What changed: added a multi-window detector that compares short-term and medium-term latency distributions, tuned thresholds based on production traffic traces, and a hysteresis guard that requires a sustained violation (configurable window + severity multiplier) before triggering canary rollout changes. Also added a new metric (perf_canary_violation_score) and dashboard panels for debugging.

How it works: the detector computes p95 latency over two windows (30s, 10m), computes an effect-size score, and only counts violations that exceed a configurable severity and persist for N consecutive short windows. Hysteresis prevents flip-flopping by requiring the effect-size to drop below a recovery threshold for M consecutive windows before clearing the violation.

Testing: unit tests for detector logic, integration tests in perf-canary lab using replayed production traces, and an end-to-end dry-run mode deployed to staging where rollouts are recorded but not executed. CI includes synthetic workloads that emulate brief spikes and sustained regressions.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary controller (10% of clusters) for 48h in dry-run, then enable enforcement with a conservative hysteresis (N=3 short windows) for 7 days while monitoring perf_canary_violation_score, alert rate, and rollback incidents.

Related: Linear ENG-8421 (perf canary improvements), ENG-8530 (observability panels), references to prior work: pr-218543, pr-224567.
